status: draft rule set; awaiting expert review
not_advice: This is a transparent, rule-based screen of which therapeutic approach could fit which mechanism, written for a biotech scout and for patient-group leaders. It is NOT medical advice, NOT a recommendation for any individual, and NOT a claim that any approach will work. 'Good fit' means only that the published mechanism matches what the approach does. Treatment decisions belong to a patient's own clinicians.

fit_scale.good: the mechanism matches what the approach does, with at least one citation
fit_scale.conditional: possible, but a named condition must be met first (variant class, dose, a missing target element, or counter-evidence)
fit_scale.poor: the mechanism points the other way, or a hard constraint blocks it
fit_scale.not_assessed: no rule applies; the mechanism profile is too thin

meta.aggregation: the WORST fit voted by any rule that fired, so one blocking rule is never averaged away
meta.citations: assessments carry citation_ids into the top-level `citations` map; each entry is a schema Evidence item whose quote was string-matched against the stored source
inputs: data/graph.json driven_by / developed_for / studies edges and gene attrs
data/derived/variants.json ClinVar variant-class mix per gene
data/raw/derive/pubmed/<PMID>.json (every quote cut from the stored record)
meta.expert_review_checklist: not yet attached; a rare-disease advisor's checklist may be added later and should record, per (disease, modality): agree/disagree with the fit, the missing condition, and anything the rule table gets backwards.

modalities.label: AAV gene replacement
modalities.what_it_does: A virus delivers an extra, working copy of the gene to neurons; the faulty copy stays.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: haploinsufficiency / loss of function with no interfering mutant protein

modalities.label: ASO / siRNA knockdown (total or allele-specific)
modalities.what_it_does: An oligonucleotide lowers the amount of the gene's RNA, either both copies or only the faulty one.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: gain of function or dominant-negative, where less of the faulty product is better

modalities.label: Transcript upregulation (TANGO/NMD- or uORF-targeting ASO, or CRISPRa)
modalities.what_it_does: A drug makes the cell read the gene's own healthy copy more efficiently instead of adding a new copy.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: haploinsufficiency with one intact allele and a targetable regulatory element

modalities.label: Chemical / pharmacological chaperone
modalities.what_it_does: A small molecule helps an unstable protein fold and reach its working place instead of being degraded.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: protein destabilization / misfolding, where the mutant protein would work if it survived

modalities.label: Symptomatic small molecule acting on the pathway (e.g. 3,4-DAP, 4-AP, cholinesterase inhibitors)
modalities.what_it_does: An existing drug pushes the weakened synapse to release more neurotransmitter per nerve impulse. It does not change the gene.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: reduced evoked release, especially at the neuromuscular junction

modalities.label: Gene editing (base / prime editing, CRISPR repair)
modalities.what_it_does: A tool rewrites the faulty DNA letter in the patient's own cells.
modalities.best_case_mechanism: a recurrent, editable variant whose effect is dominant-negative or gain of function

rules.condition: the gene's CDS does not fit a standard AAV (>4.7 kb)
rules.reason: The coding sequence is too large for one standard AAV genome, so a single-vector gene replacement is not available.
rules.caveat: Dual/split-vector and other strategies to exceed the limit exist, but add complexity and are not de-risked here.

rules.condition: haploinsufficiency or loss of function is a supported mechanism and the CDS fits AAV
rules.reason: Too little working protein from one lost or non-functional copy is the mechanism gene supplementation is designed for, and the coding sequence fits one AAV.

rules.condition: a dominant-negative effect is reported and is not flagged as a minority mechanism
rules.reason: If the mutant protein actively jams the machine, adding healthy copies may be diluted out by it, so supplementation alone may not be enough.
rules.caveat: Whether the dominant-negative reading holds for this gene is itself contested in the graph; see the driven_by edge.

rules.condition: a gain-of-function mechanism is reported for at least some variants
rules.reason: For variants that make the protein do too much, adding more of it is the wrong direction, so eligibility would have to be decided per variant.
rules.caveat: Gene supplementation is not reversible, which raises the cost of getting the variant's functional class wrong.

rules.condition: published overexpression data exist for this gene
rules.reason: Overexpression of this protein has measurable consequences in animals, so the dose window matters as much as the delivery.
rules.caveat: Dose-finding needs a biomarker of protein level; no human threshold is established for any gene in this slice.

rules.condition: a gene-replacement trial for this disease was terminated or stopped
rules.reason: A first-in-human gene-replacement trial for this disease has already been stopped, which is counter-evidence a scout must read before planning another.
rules.caveat: A stopping rule being met is not public evidence about why; treat the reason as unknown.

rules.condition: a gain-of-function mechanism is reported and is not flagged as a minority mechanism
rules.reason: When the faulty product does too much, lowering it is the matching direction, and ASO knockdown has done this in a gain-of-function epilepsy model.
rules.caveat: Benefit was shown in a different gene and species; nothing of the kind has been tried in this slice.

rules.condition: a gain-of-function mechanism is reported but only for a minority of variants
rules.reason: Only a minority of published variants in this gene act by gain of function, so knockdown would fit that subset and work against everyone else.
rules.caveat: Variant-level functional classification does not exist for this gene yet (gap:variant-level-mechanism-map).

rules.condition: a dominant-negative effect is reported
rules.reason: Silencing only the faulty copy is the standard answer to a dominant-negative protein, and has been achieved for a dominant-negative substitution in another disease.
rules.caveat: Allele-specific targeting of a single-nucleotide change is hard and has to be built per variant.

rules.condition: haploinsufficiency is a supported mechanism and no gain of function is reported
rules.reason: The cell already makes too little of this protein, so lowering it further (total knockdown) works against the mechanism.

rules.condition: ClinVar shows no residue with two or more distinct pathogenic alleles
rules.reason: No recurrent hotspot appears in the pathogenic records for this gene, so an allele-specific drug would be a one-family (n-of-1) design rather than a reusable one.

rules.condition: haploinsufficiency is a supported mechanism
rules.reason: Making the intact copy produce more protein is the mechanism-matched approach to haploinsufficiency, and both ASO and CRISPRa versions have rescued haploinsufficient animals.

rules.condition: always: the approach needs a targetable element in THIS gene
rules.reason: Each of these drugs needs a specific handle in the gene itself: a non-productive splicing event, a uORF, or a workable promoter/enhancer. Whether one exists here is not established.
rules.caveat: A uORF-blocking result has failed to reproduce in independent hands, so a candidate element is not a candidate drug.

rules.condition: protein destabilization or a dominant-negative effect is reported
rules.reason: Upregulation that is not allele-specific raises the mutant transcript too, and for an aggregating or interfering protein more mutant may offset more wild type.
rules.caveat: A promoter- or splicing-level drug cannot currently distinguish the two alleles.

rules.condition: a gain-of-function mechanism is reported for some variants
rules.reason: For gain-of-function variants, raising expression is the wrong direction, so eligibility would be per variant.

rules.condition: protein destabilization / misfolding is a reported mechanism
rules.reason: A chaperone's whole purpose is to stabilise a protein that would work if it were not degraded, which is exactly what the destabilization evidence for this gene describes.

rules.condition: most pathogenic ClinVar records for this gene are null-like (truncating, splice or copy-number)
rules.reason: A chaperone can only act where there is a mutant protein to stabilise, and most pathogenic records for this gene remove the protein instead, so the approach reaches a minority of patients.
rules.caveat: The share below is a share of ClinVar records, not of patients; recurrent variants are counted once.

rules.condition: no destabilization mechanism is reported for this gene
rules.reason: Nothing in the atlas links this gene's disease to an unstable or misfolded protein, so there is no stated target for a chaperone.

rules.condition: always, when a chaperone is on the table
rules.reason: Generic chemical chaperones are not selective: for this class the required concentrations and possible toxicity are the stated reason to look for a targeted molecule instead.
rules.caveat: Whether the benefit comes from correcting the mutant or from helping the wild-type protein traffic is unresolved, which changes who could benefit.

rules.condition: the disease has a neuromuscular-junction presentation (congenital myasthenic syndrome)
rules.reason: For presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndromes these drugs are the established symptomatic option, and the choice follows the genetic defect.
rules.caveat: Benefit is symptomatic: it does not change the course of the brain phenotype.

rules.condition: release is reduced but the presentation is central (no NMJ phenotype)
rules.reason: Pushing more release could compensate a weakened synapse, and single-patient and human-neuron reports exist in this family, but no controlled trial does.
rules.caveat: Evidence in the central presentation is a case report and a cell model, not a trial.

rules.condition: a gain-of-function or excess-spontaneous-release variant class exists in this gene
rules.reason: The same gene contains variants that increase release, and for those a release-boosting drug points the wrong way, so variant class has to be established first.
rules.caveat: Aminopyridines have a narrow therapeutic range and a dose-related seizure risk, which matters in a population that already has epilepsy.

rules.condition: no drug of this class has been reported for this gene
rules.reason: The fit here comes from the shared pathway only; no report names this gene, so it rests on the family argument rather than on gene-specific evidence.

rules.condition: always, for every gene in this slice
rules.reason: Editing in the brain is attractive because neurons do not divide, so one correction could last, but no editing programme exists for any disease in this slice.
rules.caveat: Delivery, per-variant design and off-target assessment are all unsolved for these genes; treat this as a research direction, not a pipeline.

rules.condition: a dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism is reported
rules.reason: Correcting or disabling the faulty allele is the one approach that addresses an interfering protein without adding more protein.

rules.condition: the graph records a gene-disease validity or functional-evidence gap for this gene
rules.reason: The gene-disease link or the mechanism itself is flagged as a gap in the atlas, so no modality can score better than conditional until that is settled.
rules.caveat: This caps the fit; it is not evidence against the approach.

rules.condition: ClinVar shows no recurrent pathogenic residue in this gene
rules.reason: Without a recurrent variant, each family needs its own editor, which no current development path supports for an ultra-rare disease.
